Disaster management involves preparedness, mitigation, response, and recovery efforts to reduce the impact of such natural hazards on human life and property. Coastal regions are particularly vulnerable to cyclones due to storm surges and flooding.

back2basics.text: Summits between heads of major powers are diplomatic meetings aimed at managing bilateral and multilateral relations, addressing conflicts, and promoting peace. These meetings often focus on issues like nuclear disarmament, trade, and regional conflicts. Strategic stability refers to maintaining a balance of power to prevent conflict escalation, especially among nuclear-armed states.

back2basics.text: The Wholesale Price Index measures the average change in prices of goods at the wholesale level before they reach consumers. Inflation is the rate at which prices increase over time, affecting purchasing power. WPI inflation often signals future changes in consumer prices and influences monetary policy decisions such as interest rate adjustments by the central bank.

back2basics.text: Just Transition refers to shifting to a low-carbon economy in a way that is fair and inclusive, addressing social and economic impacts on workers and communities. Nature-based climate solutions use ecosystem conservation and restoration to mitigate climate change by enhancing carbon storage and ecosystem resilience.

2026-11-17-am-c6e52fd3b9.deck: At COP31 in Antalya, India advocated for a country-driven Just Transition Mechanism emphasizing finance, technology transfer, and capacity building for developing countries. The event also highlighted India's tiger conservation as a nature-based climate solution strengthening ecosystem resilience and livelihoods.

body.label: Just Transition Mechanism
body.text: India called for a two-tier, Party-guided Just Transition Mechanism that respects national sovereignty and diverse national circumstances, focusing on practical, country-driven implementation.

body.label: Key focus areas
body.text: The mechanism should address employment, social protection, adaptation, poverty eradication, energy access, and sustainable development with adequate finance, technology transfer, and capacity building.

body.label: Integration across policies
body.text: India emphasized integrating just transition considerations across adaptation, livelihoods, and development planning, citing its sub-national heat action and renewable energy expansion plans.

body.label: Distinct roles
body.text: India proposed distinct roles for the UAE Just Transition Work Programme (dialogue platform) and the proposed Mechanism (practical support via technical assistance and cooperation).

sections.heading: What did India propose at COP31 regarding climate transition?

body.label: Ecosystem protection
body.text: Big cat conservation helps protect carbon-rich ecosystems like forests, grasslands, wetlands, and mountains, which store carbon and prevent emissions from habitat degradation.

body.label: India's tiger conservation model
body.text: India's Project Tiger, supported by legislation and the National Tiger Conservation Authority, has increased tiger population to 3,682 in 2022, protecting 58 Tiger Reserves spanning about 85,000 sq. km.

body.label: Ecosystem services
body.text: Tiger reserves provide vital ecosystem services including carbon sequestration, water purification, soil conservation, groundwater recharge, and support over 600 rivers.

body.label: Community involvement
body.text: Community participation and sustainable livelihood initiatives have made tiger conservation inclusive and a driver of green employment, generating about 6 million man-days annually.

body.label: International collaboration
body.text: The International Big Cat Alliance, envisioned by India's Prime Minister, facilitates knowledge exchange and cooperation for global big cat species recovery.

sections.heading: How does big cat conservation relate to climate change mitigation?

body.label: Slow finance delivery
body.text: Developing countries face slow and insufficient climate finance despite pledges to increase funding to $300 billion per year by 2035.

body.label: Geopolitical and economic hurdles
body.text: Western governments prioritize national security and inflation concerns, reducing urgency and funding for climate action amid global conflicts.

body.label: Administrative barriers
body.text: Technical hurdles and complex procedures limit small states' capacity to access climate finance effectively.

body.label: Calls for implementation
body.text: COP31 emphasized accelerating implementation of existing pledges with finance that is faster, simpler, and fairer, rather than setting new targets.

body.label: Innovative funding
body.text: Some small nations pledged their own funds to spur richer countries to match contributions and invest in nature-based solutions like seagrass restoration.

back2basics.concept: Role of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)
back2basics.text: The CAG is a constitutional authority responsible for auditing the accounts of the Union and State governments and public sector entities. It ensures public money is used efficiently and transparently, thus strengthening accountability. The CAG reports to the Parliament and State Legislatures, helping them oversee government financial management.

2026-11-17-am-f8bb944e4e.deck: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India has emphasized technology adoption and institutional reforms to strengthen public accountability and align audits with national development goals. This is important for UPSC aspirants to understand the evolving role of constitutional bodies in governance and transparency.

body: Technological reforms like AI tools and data-led audits have shortened audit cycles and improved data security.
Thematic audits on ‘Ease of Doing Business’ and ‘Ease of Living’ align audit focus with national development goals.
Breaking departmental silos and expanding audits to local bodies enhance comprehensive oversight.
Capacity building through AI training equips officials to handle modern audit challenges.
structure.conclusion: These reforms strengthen the CAG’s ability to ensure transparency and foster public trust in governance.
structure.intro: The CAG plays a key role in public accountability by auditing government finances and operations.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the recent reforms and initiatives by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India:
1. The CAG has initiated pan-India horizontal audits on themes like ‘Ease of Doing Business’ and ‘Ease of Living’.
2. The CAG has reduced the audit cycle time from six to eight months to three months through data-led audits and AI tools.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: A trap could be confusing the audit themes or the timeline of audit cycle reduction; both statements are supported by the evidence.

pyq.question: In the light of Satyam Scandal (2009), discuss the changes brought in corporate governance to ensure transparency and accountability.
pyq.why: This question on corporate governance reforms relates to the CAG’s role in ensuring transparency and accountability, which is enhanced by the recent technology and audit reforms.

body.label: Breaking departmental silos
body.text: The CAG has started working across departmental silos to conduct audits covering cross-sectoral issues, enabling a more integrated audit approach.

body.label: Thematic audits
body.text: Audits now focus on themes like ‘Ease of Living’ and ‘Ease of Doing Business’, aligning with national development goals and assessing reforms at the grassroots level.

body.label: Focus on local bodies
body.text: The CAG has expanded audits of local governance, prioritizing quality of accounts, uniform grant reporting, timely audits, and coverage of the top 500 cities.

sections.heading: What reforms has the CAG implemented to strengthen public accountability?

body.label: AI tools for audits
body.text: The CAG is developing audit-specific artificial intelligence tools to enhance data security and efficiency in audits.

body.label: Data-led audits
body.text: Pilot projects using data-led audits for establishment expenditure, social-sector Direct Benefit Transfers, and public works reduced the audit cycle from six to eight months to three months.

body.label: Capacity building
body.text: The institution is investing in developing officials skilled in AI through the AI Champions and AI Enablers programme, involving collaboration with start-ups.

sections.heading: How is technology being used by the CAG to improve audit processes?

body.label: Audit reports and recommendations
body.text: In the last year, the CAG tabled 40 Union government and 174 State government audit reports, making 3,742 audit recommendations, with nearly one-third accepted.

body.label: Units audited
body.text: Over 34,000 units were audited and more than 27,000 inspection reports issued, covering Union and State governments, PSUs, autonomous bodies, and externally aided projects.

body.label: Horizontal audits
body.text: Pan-India horizontal audits include ‘Ease of Doing Business’ for MSMEs and urban mobility audits in 101 major cities under the ‘Ease of Living’ theme.

sections.heading: What is the scale and impact of the CAG’s audit work?
